flashcard_questions.q: What is a sacrament in Christianity?
flashcard_questions.a: An outward sign of an inward, spiritual blessing from God.

flashcard_questions.q: How many sacraments do Roman Catholic and Orthodox Christians recognise?
Why do most Protestants recognise only two sacraments?
flashcard_questions.a: Only baptism and Holy Communion were instituted directly by Jesus.

flashcard_questions.q: What does the Latin word “sacramentum” mean?
How is water used in infant baptism?
flashcard_questions.a: It is poured over the baby’s head three times.

flashcard_questions.q: What does infant baptism remove, according to Catholic teaching?
flashcard_questions.a: Original sin, inherited from Adam and Eve.

flashcard_questions.q: What does full immersion symbolise in believers’ baptism?
flashcard_questions.a: Dying to the old sinful life and rising to new life in Christ.

flashcard_questions.q: Why do Baptists reject infant baptism?
flashcard_questions.a: They argue that babies cannot understand the commitment being made.

flashcard_questions.q: Which two groups do not practise baptism at all?
What did Jesus say as he broke bread at the Last Supper?
flashcard_questions.a: “This is my body given for you; do this in remembrance of me.”

flashcard_questions.q: What is transubstantiation in Catholic teaching?
flashcard_questions.a: The bread and wine literally become the body and blood of Christ.

flashcard_questions.q: How do most Protestants understand the bread and wine?
flashcard_questions.a: As symbols taken in remembrance of Jesus’s sacrifice.

flashcard_questions.q: What is the Orthodox celebration of Holy Communion called?
What does the Greek word “Eucharist” mean?

notes: 15 cards: 4 term→definition (sacrament, sacramentum, transubstantiation, Eucharist), 4 denomination→position (seven vs two, Protestant symbolism, Orthodox liturgy, Salvation Army and Quakers), 4 practice→meaning (pouring water, original sin, immersion, Baptist objection), 2 belief→source (Last Supper words), 1 attribution.
